database_summary: This SQLite database models motorsport (Formula 1 style) data: circuits, races, constructors, drivers, timed events (lap times, pit stops, qualifying), race results and standings, plus a set of *_ext tables that provide enriched or denormalized attributes and stats. Core event facts (lap_times, pit_stops, results, sprint_results, qualifying) are at the per-race/per-driver (and often per-lap) grain. Several small lookup/dimension tables (circuits, constructors, drivers, status, seasons, short_* ) provide descriptive attributes. There are two parallel sets of tables: primary normalized tables and *_ext denormalized variants containing additional derived fields and textual representations. Be cautious joining fact tables to each other (can multiply rows) and to constructors/drivers when multiple rows per entity per race exist (e.g., results vs. driver_standings).

accepted.name: race_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  url,
  fp1_date,
  fp1_time,
  fp2_date,
  fp2_time,
  fp3_date,
  fp3_time,
  quali_date,
  quali_time,
  sprint_date,
  sprint_time
FROM races
accepted.description: Normalized projection of races with canonical key and descriptive attributes. Use this as a stable race dimension when joining facts — preserves race identifiers and common attributes (year, round, circuit_id, name, date, time). | Use for: List races by year/round/circuit; Join races to results/qualifying/pit stops; Filter races by date or by having sprint/quali

accepted.name: driver_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  driver_ref,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers
accepted.description: Normalized driver dimension projection exposing identity columns suitable for joins and reporting (keeps forename/surname/code/number and dob). Use whenever driver descriptive attributes are needed. | Use for: Lookup driver details by id or name; Join driver attributes to lap_times, results, pit_stops

accepted.name: constructor_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructor_id,
  constructor_ref,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors
accepted.description: Constructor/team dimension projection preserving identifiers and descriptive attributes for joins and reporting. | Use for: Join constructor info to results/constructor_standings/constructor_results; List constructors and their nationality

accepted.name: lap_times_measure
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  lap,
  position,
  time,
  milliseconds
FROM lap_times
accepted.description: Clean projection of lap_times with numeric milliseconds and original time string. Useful for per-lap analyses, pace calculations, and joining to driver/race dimensions. | Use for: Per-lap fastest times, average lap time per driver/race; Compare lap times across drivers or laps

accepted.name: pit_stops_measure
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  stop,
  lap,
  time,
  duration,
  milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
accepted.description: Projection of pit_stops events preserving per-stop grain and numeric milliseconds. Use for pit strategy and stop-duration analyses. | Use for: Count pit stops per driver/race; Average pit stop duration by team/year

accepted.name: results_fact
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  result_id,
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  constructor_id,
  number,
  grid,
  position,
  position_text,
  position_order,
  points,
  laps,
  time,
  milliseconds,
  fastest_lap,
  rank,
  fastest_lap_time,
  fastest_lap_speed,
  status_id
FROM results
accepted.description: Projection of race results preserving primary identifiers and key measures (positions, points, laps, milliseconds, fastest lap info). Use as the canonical results fact table for downstream analyses. | Use for: Podium finishers, points per race/driver/constructor; Join race results to lap_times or pit_stops for deeper analysis

accepted.name: qualifying_grid
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualify_id,
  q.race_id,
  q.driver_id,
  q.constructor_id,
  q.number,
  q.position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  d.driver_ref,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name AS name
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON q.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON q.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
accepted.description: Denormalized qualifying result with driver and constructor attributes. One row per qualify_id (driver in a race qualifying). Useful when analyzing grid performance with driver/constructor context. | Use for: Compare qualifying position to race grid/results; Driver/constructor qualifying performance

accepted.name: driver_season_points
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year,
  res.driver_id,
  SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
GROUP BY r.year, res.driver_id
accepted.description: Aggregate points per driver per year (season) by summing results.points across races. Useful for season totals, ranking drivers by season, or trend analysis. Grain: one row per year + driver. | Use for: Season standings by driver (points per year); Compare drivers' season totals or compute averages per race

accepted.name: constructor_season_points
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year,
  res.constructor_id,
  SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
GROUP BY r.year, res.constructor_id
accepted.description: Aggregate points per constructor per year by summing results.points across races. Grain: one row per year + constructor. Useful for constructor championship tallies and season comparisons. | Use for: Constructor championship points by season; Rank constructors by year

accepted.name: fastest_lap_per_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.race_id,
  lt.driver_id,
  lt.lap,
  MIN(lt.milliseconds) AS fastest_milliseconds
FROM lap_times lt
GROUP BY lt.race_id
accepted.description: Per-race fastest lap by selecting the minimum milliseconds among lap_times. Outputs the driving row (race_id, driver_id, lap) with the fastest milliseconds. Use for identifying which driver set the fastest lap in a race (based on lap_times table). | Use for: Which driver set the fastest lap in each race?; Compare fastest lap milliseconds across races

accepted.name: driver_lap_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS best_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds,
  COUNT(*) AS laps_completed
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Aggregate lap statistics per race and driver: best lap (min milliseconds), avg milliseconds and lap count. Useful for comparing driver pace within a race. | Use for: Driver pace summaries per race; Identify drivers with consistent lap times or highest avg speed

accepted.name: driver_season_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  dsp.year,
  dsp.driver_id,
  dsp.total_points,
  dsp.races_participated,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dsp.year ORDER BY dsp.total_points DESC) AS driver_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.driver_id,
    SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
    COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
  GROUP BY r.year, res.driver_id
) dsp
accepted.description: Season ranking of drivers by total points. Uses a window rank over year partition to provide a driver_rank column; keep year, driver_id and total_points so downstream queries can filter rank <= K. Grain: one row per year + driver. | Use for: Top-k drivers by season; Filter drivers with rank <= K per year

accepted.name: constructor_season_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  csp.year,
  csp.constructor_id,
  csp.total_points,
  csp.races_participated,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY csp.year ORDER BY csp.total_points DESC) AS constructor_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.constructor_id,
    SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
    COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
  GROUP BY r.year, res.constructor_id
) csp
accepted.description: Season ranking of constructors by total points. Produces constructor_rank for each year; useful for selecting top constructors or comparing relative positions across seasons. | Use for: Top-k constructors by season; Compare constructor ranks across years

accepted.name: race_pitstop_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_stop_count,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Summary of pit stop activity per race and driver: total pit stops and average/median milliseconds. Useful for pit strategy comparisons. Note: SQLite doesn't have MEDIAN built-in; this exposes avg and count which are widely useful. | Use for: Identify drivers with most pit stops in a race; Compare average pit stop durations across drivers/teams

accepted.name: results_with_driver_constructor
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  res.result_id,
  res.race_id,
  res.driver_id,
  d.driver_ref,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  res.constructor_id,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name AS name,
  res.number,
  res.grid,
  res.position,
  res.points,
  res.laps,
  res.milliseconds,
  res.fastest_lap
FROM results res
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON res.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON res.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
accepted.description: Denormalized race results joined with driver and constructor descriptive attributes. One row per result_id. Use when reporting results with human-readable names and codes. | Use for: Result listings with driver/constructor names; Filter results by driver name, constructor, or grid position
